clue.text: Horrified at being cut by jagged gash

indicators.note: a word being cut by another has that other word placed inside it
jagged suggests the letters of the following word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at the sight of a ragged wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' suggests a wound, but here a word is cut open by the scrambled gash; 'jagged' and 'being cut by' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone struck with shock and dismay.

clue.text: Variety of winged duck

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters that follow take a new arrangement

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A bird-book entry naming a kind of duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' shuffles WINGED with O, a cricketer's duck (a score of nothing). Read as a whole, the clue also describes the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird is a species of dabbling duck, so the whole clue serves as its description.

clue.text: He makes little or no effort to conserve energy

definitions.text: He makes little or no effort to conserve energy

parts.words: He makes little or no effort to conserve energy
parts.note: a sly description of an idle person, as though his idleness were an energy-saving policy

explanation.surface: A man who saves energy by hardly lifting a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle person is someone who avoids exertion, which the clue presents as conservation of effort.

clue.text: Fierce storm on the coast of Brazil

indicators.note: to storm is to rage, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent tempest hits the Brazilian shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city lies on Brazil's north-eastern Atlantic shore.

clue.text: Medical men investing in a foreign currency

indicators.note: investing here means clothing or surrounding, so the doctors wrap round what follows

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doctors put money into an overseas currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' is used in its old sense of enclosing (as in investing a city), not putting money in.
explanation.definitionFit: These coins are the money of several Middle Eastern and Balkan countries.

clue.text: Its owner is glad to wag it!

definitions.text: Its owner is glad to wag it!

parts.words: Its owner is glad to wag it!
parts.note: the owner who wags it is a happy pet, and the thing wagged is the end of that animal

explanation.surface: A pet owner cheerfully waving something about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'owner' suggests a person, but the owner is the animal itself; the answer is also the name of a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy hound's rear appendage is the thing it wags.

clue.text: Famous member of Kelly gang about to turn in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ned Kelly led the Australian outlaw Kelly gang

indicators.note: about signals turning the little word round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-known bushranger is about to hand himself over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the little word round before 'in' puts it inside. Ned Kelly was a notorious Australian outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrated or well known is famous.

clue.text: He won notoriety by claiming to know what was good for the Cesarewitch

definitions.text: He won notoriety by claiming to know what was good for the Cesarewitch

parts.words: He won notoriety by claiming to know what was good for the Cesarewitch
parts.note: reads like a racing tipster boasting about the Cesarewitch horse race, but the Cesarewitch is the heir of the Russian tsar, whose illness a mystic claimed to treat

explanation.surface: A tipster became infamous for claiming inside knowledge of a big horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cesarewitch is a famous Newmarket horse race, but here it is the Tsarevich Alexei, whose haemophilia the monk claimed to heal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siberian mystic gained infamy at court through his supposed power to heal the tsar's heir.

clue.text: Showed annoyance in grating nutmeg?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a grid is a grating of crossed bars
mace is the spice made from the outer covering of the nutmeg seed

explanation.surface: A cook pulls a face while grating nutmeg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like a verb but is the noun GRID, with MACE put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a twisted face is a way to show displeasure.

clue.text: He has little to say about others

definitions.text: He has little to say about others

parts.words: He has little to say about others
parts.note: a self-absorbed talker who only speaks about himself, so he says little of anyone else

explanation.surface: A man who keeps quiet about other people.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like discretion, but he is silent about others only because he talks about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person talks constantly of himself rather than other people.

clue.text: Some Greek inwardly fuming?

indicators.note: inwardly says something sits on the inside of the other word

parts.note: some can mean any, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A Greek is quietly seething.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is ANY, with GR placed 'inwardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuming means seething with rage.

clue.text: Amazingly deft tout I provided with equipment

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something astonishing has happened to the following letters, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nimble ticket tout kits himself out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' rearranges DEFT TOUT I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be supplied with gear or furnishings is to be kitted up.

clue.text: 10 reaction that is inwardly right

indicators.note: inwardly puts one piece on the inside of the other

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An angry response that is right at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 refers to 10 Across (fuming); the reaction of someone fuming is wrath.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is the response of someone who is furious.

clue.text: Became captain of the side and did some bowling

definitions.meaning: to assume control, as of a team
in cricket a bowler who bowls a set of six balls has had an over

explanation.surface: A cricketer was made captain and also bowled for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled by one player.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming command is one sense; a cricketer bowling a set of six balls is another.

clue.text: I occupied a factory producing oxidised indigo…

parts.note: workers who occupy their workplace in protest stage a sit-in

explanation.surface: Workers occupy a dye works making indigo derivatives.
explanation.walkthrough: A sit-in is a protest in which workers occupy their premises.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-red compound is obtained by oxidation of the blue dye.

clue.text: American soldiers captivated by Molly's revolutionary piece of deductive reasoning

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside, so the soldiers are enclosed
revolutionary means turned round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: the name Molly with its possessive S
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: US troops are enchanted by a radical woman's logic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reads as political but means turned backwards (giving SYLLOM); 'captivated by' then encloses the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument drawing a conclusion from two premises is classic deductive logic.

clue.text: Tired of being a footman?

parts.note: reads as weary of serving as a liveried servant, but taken literally a foot-man walks everywhere and his limbs ache

explanation.surface: A servant has had enough of his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footman' suggests a servant, but read as someone on foot it explains why his limbs are tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exhausted from walking far has limbs that are worn out.

clue.text: … before some of the

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '... before some of the (3)': 'before' defines the answer, but the hidden-word fodder after 'the' is cut short in the OCR, so the run of letters cannot be shown

clue.text: Does it patchily show lack of caution?

definitions.text: Does it patchily show lack of caution?

parts.words: Does it patchily show lack of caution?
parts.note: a skin eruption shows in patches, so the state of having one is offered as a word for recklessness

explanation.surface: A question about whether recklessness shows in patches.
explanation.walkthrough: A rash is a patchy skin eruption, and being rash means reckless: the clue joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Recklessness is the quality of acting hastily without care.

clue.text: Knowing how to get to places quickly

definitions.meaning: British slang for sharp and streetwise

definitions.text: how to get to places quickly
definitions.meaning: travelling by air is the fastest way to reach somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone who knows the quickest routes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing' here is the British slang sense of shrewd, as in a fly customer.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang adjective means shrewd; the verb means to travel by air or rush.

clue.text: Amused sort of jellyfish

indicators.note: sort of means a version, so the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A jellyfish that seems to be enjoying itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amused' looks like it describes the creature, but 'sort of' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In zoology this word names the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a cnidarian.

clue.text: Tout a bet out Lincoln?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Tout a bet for Lincoln?': the wordplay needs 'T out' (T removed from A BET), but the OCR joined it into the single word 'Tout', which cannot be both the letter and the indicator

clue.text: Fish that catch other fish

parts.note: reads as people who fish, but these are predatory sea creatures that lure prey with a lure on the head

explanation.surface: Predatory fish hunting smaller ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural names both people who fish with rod and line and the lure-bearing fish that hunt other fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea predators with a fleshy lure take their name from rod-and-line fishermen.

clue.text: Juvenile delinquents going round North America's infertile regions

indicators.note: going round says the delinquents surround the next piece

parts.note: bad lads are young troublemakers

explanation.surface: Young offenders roaming the barren terrain of North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North America' looks like one phrase, but North gives only N.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren eroded terrain in the western United States carries this name.

clue.text: A wrongly named fillet

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the word are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A headband given the wrong name.
explanation.walkthrough: A fillet here is a band for the hair, not a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland or band worn round the head is an old word for a hair ribbon.

clue.text: Beer that has been diluted and cast out?

indicators.note: out puts the throw on the outside of the conjunction

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watered-down ale that has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast out' reads as a phrase, but cast is SHY, which goes 'out'(side) AND.
explanation.definitionFit: This drink is ale mixed with lemonade, so it is weakened.

clue.text: Change the fellows who operate the points system?

parts.note: to switch is to change
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Replacing the staff who run a scoring system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points system' suggests scoring, but points are railway junction switches.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway workers who move the points that divert trains do this job.

clue.text: A slatternly female brought up in Oklahoma

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a slut is an old word for a slovenly woman

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman raised in the Sooner State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses A SLUT as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Arkansas River is in that US state.

clue.text: Give a specious attractiveness to a Verdi heroine

parts.note: to gild is to make something look better than it is

explanation.surface: Glamorising an opera heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto's daughter is the heroine of that opera.

clue.text: Agreed sum drawn out?

definitions.meaning: a sum counted up, as a score totted

explanation.surface: A sum stretched out until everyone agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn out' suggests lengthened, but means drawn up, as a total is reckoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that correspond have matched; a score totted up has been counted.

clue.text: Made sure, in a way, what the size was

indicators.note: in a way means in a different manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checked the dimensions to be certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges MADE SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking dimensions determines how big a thing is.

clue.text: No way to go through a congested area down

definitions.text: No way to go through a congested area down

parts.words: No way to go through a congested area down
parts.note: a road that avoids passing through a busy place; the final word is the Down heading caught in the OCR

explanation.surface: A road that steers clear of a crowded town.
explanation.walkthrough: The road is a way, but its purpose is to avoid going through the crowded centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A road built round a town lets traffic avoid its crowded centre.
